rows.name: mistral_telecom_R0_final
rows.rationale: The admitted ERROR label agrees with gold but charges no prior user request and no suspension investigation. Original h32 explicitly requests restoration and h9/h10 is a successful line lookup showing Suspended and the expired contract. R0 selected eight policy sources and no history, so absence from this retrieved subset proves neither absent request nor absent check. q7 has no blanket rule requiring every call to respond to an explicit user request. Correct label, wrong source-based cause; the governing expiry prohibition was read but its specific observed state was not.

rows.name: mistral_telecom_R1_final
rows.rationale: First plan fails whole-round gap namespace validation before any read or search. It supplies d9 in policy_sources although declarations are not selectable catalog entries, and h8/h10/h34/h0 as target_sources though only current t0 is an allowed target. h10 is named as a candidate but never read. Final raw ERROR uses NO_POLICY_RETRIEVED pseudo-policy IDs, charges missing status/ownership checks from empty retrieved history and is rejected ADMISSION:NORM_REFERENCE_INVALID. This is a controller/plan technical blockage plus an unsupported final argument, not an admitted semantic result of recursive retrieval.

rows.name: mistral_telecom_coverage_final
rows.rationale: The generic one-shot literal target-operand/chronology coverage selector reads q7/q17 and customer, bill and line call/receipt pairs, including h10. Final admitted ERROR correctly binds t0 L1002 to the 2025-01-31 contract date against q7 clock 2025-02-25 and rejects Paid as a waiver. It also misattributes the specific expired-contract escalation instruction to q7 rather than q17, a peripheral norm-scope defect. No gain over already-correct I4; correct causal repair relative to R0 on this same known positive, without testing recursive execution.
